headline: Open deep-learning tools automate quantitative trait extraction from plant images
label: Deep Learning Plant Phenotyping
summary: Four openly released phenotyping tools dated 2026-01-21 extend deep-learning image analysis to root, fruit, and temporal plant traits.
synthesis: The common thread is deep-learning image analysis for quantitative plant phenotyping, with openly released software as the central contribution. pyRootHair applies machine learning to extract root hair traits from root microscope images, processing over 600 images at high throughput. ChronoRoot 2.0 uses nnUNet multi-class segmentation to track six plant structures over time in 2D phenotyping of Arabidopsis. The almond workflow provides an open Python pipeline for fruit morphology, color, and morphometrics, reporting segmentation error below 1% across more than 25,000 kernels. What is new is the emphasis on openly released tooling for automated trait extraction. GridScore NEXT is adjacent: an open-source offline app for phenotype data capture with validation rules and barcodes, addressing data collection rather than segmentation.
